entries.title: Don't use Bing or web results in Windows Search
entries.description: Applies the Windows Search policies that stop Windows from sending typed queries to Bing and from showing web results in the search box.
entries.rationale: Windows Search otherwise sends what you type to Bing and mixes web results with local files; local file, app and settings search is unaffected. Both policy values are absent by default.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Search\Don't search the web or display web results in Search

sideEffects: The 'Search the web' rows and Bing web results disappear from Windows Search; only local apps, files and settings are shown.
ConnectedSearchUseWeb is officially documented for Enterprise/Education; on Home and Pro the web-results removal relies on the legacy DisableWebSearch policy.

entries.title: Turn off search highlights
entries.description: Turns off the Bing-driven 'highlights' content (trending topics and events) shown in the search box and search home.
entries.rationale: Search highlights fetch dynamic content from Microsoft/Bing; turning them off keeps the search box static. Purely cosmetic and nothing depends on it. This is the per-user Settings toggle, so it also works on Home; the equivalent machine policy (EnableDynamicContentInWSB) is Pro and above.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Search\Allow search highlights

sideEffects: The search box and search home no longer show trending or highlight content.

entries.title: Disable Cortana (policy)
entries.description: Applies the AllowCortana=0 policy so the legacy Cortana assistant cannot run and cannot drive search behaviours.
entries.rationale: Cortana was removed as an inbox app in Windows 11 23H2, but the policy remains and still gates a few older search behaviours. No functional loss on modern builds. The policy value is absent by default.
sideEffects: On 23H2 and later Cortana is already gone, so this policy is largely a no-op and harmless.

entries.title: Turn off search history on this device
entries.description: Stops Windows Search from storing your recent searches on this device.
entries.rationale: Recent-search history is kept locally and suggested in the search box; disabling it removes that on-device record. Search itself keeps working.
sideEffects: Recent searches are no longer suggested in the search box.

entries.title: Turn off cloud content search
entries.description: Applies AllowCloudSearch=0 so Windows Search does not query Microsoft-account or work-account cloud content (OneDrive, SharePoint, Outlook).
entries.rationale: Cloud content search sends queries to Microsoft/365 services to surface cloud files in Start; disabling it keeps search local. The policy value is absent by default.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Search\Allow Cloud Search

sideEffects: OneDrive, SharePoint and Outlook cloud results no longer appear in Windows Search.

entries.title: Turn off Windows Copilot (legacy policy)
entries.description: Applies the per-user TurnOffWindowsCopilot policy that disabled the 2023 Copilot sidebar.
entries.rationale: Stops the legacy Copilot pane from appearing. Microsoft has deprecated this policy: the new Microsoft Copilot app is a separate package, so on 24H2 and later it is largely a no-op but remains harmless. The policy value is absent by default.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: User Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Copilot\Turn off Windows Copilot

sideEffects: Deprecated control for the 2023 Copilot sidebar; on Windows 11 24H2 and later, where Copilot is a separate app, it has little or no effect.

entries.title: Hide the Copilot taskbar button
entries.description: Hides the Copilot button on the taskbar (Windows 11 22H2/23H2).
entries.rationale: Removes the taskbar entry point for Copilot. Cosmetic; on newer builds the button was already removed, so the setting is a harmless no-op there.
sideEffects: Applies to the 22H2/23H2 taskbar Copilot button; on newer builds, where the button was removed, it has no effect.

entries.title: Disable Click to Do
entries.description: Applies the DisableClickToDo policy that turns off Click to Do screen OCR and entity extraction (Win+Q / Win+click).
entries.rationale: Click to Do runs on-device AI over whatever is on screen to extract text and entities; disabling it removes those entry points. Only meaningful on Copilot+ PCs. The policy value is absent by default.
sideEffects: Click to Do entry points in the Snipping Tool and Start are removed. Does not affect Click to Do surfaced inside Recall.

entries.title: Disable Paint AI features
entries.description: Applies the Paint policies that hide Cocreator, Generative fill and Image Creator.
entries.rationale: These Paint features send prompts and images to Microsoft's generative-AI service; the policies hide the buttons. Ordinary Paint editing is unaffected. The policy values are absent by default.
sideEffects: The Cocreator, Generative fill and Image Creator buttons are hidden in Paint.

entries.title: Disable Notepad AI features
entries.description: Applies the Notepad DisableAIFeatures policy that hides the Rewrite and Summarize features (which call Copilot).
entries.rationale: Notepad's Rewrite/Summarize send text to Copilot; the policy removes the AI menu. Plain text editing is unaffected. The policy value is absent by default.
sideEffects: This registry value is not documented by Microsoft; it ships with the Notepad Store app's ADMX and is community-verified (Win11Debloat).

entries.title: Remap the Copilot key away from Copilot
entries.description: Sets the Copilot hardware key (or Win+C) to launch a chosen app instead of Copilot; the example value targets Microsoft 365 (Office).
entries.rationale: Pressing the Copilot key otherwise opens Copilot and can send context to the cloud; remapping points it at a local or chosen app. Change the AUMID to your preferred app. The policy value is absent by default.
sideEffects: The Copilot key (or Win+C) opens the specified app instead of Copilot. The example value targets Microsoft 365 (Office); if that app is not installed the key does nothing until you set an installed app's AUMID.

entries.title: Turn off the activity feed (policy)
entries.description: Applies EnableActivityFeed=0 to stop Windows from building the local activity feed (the Timeline store).
entries.rationale: The activity feed is the local store behind Timeline and cross-device resume; disabling it stops that collection. Complements the activity-history publish and upload policies. The policy value is absent by default.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\OS Policies\Enables activity feed

sideEffects: Some 'recent activity' surfaces (for example Phone Link 'continue' or activity-based providers) may lose data. The Timeline UI is already removed in Windows 11.
